title: [narrowed from a-wired-provider-with-no-key-is-silent-capacity-loss] A WIRED PROVIDER WITH NO KEY IS SILENT CAPACITY LOS
description:
[narrowed from a-wired-provider-with-no-key-is-silent-capacity-loss] A WIRED PROVIDER WITH NO KEY IS SILENT CAPACITY LOSS, AND NOTHING IN THE SUBSTRATE REPORTS IT. llm-resolver-vessel/src/index.ts builds its OpenAI-wire provider clients once at module load: `const key = cleanEnv(process.env[p.apiKeyEnv]) ?? p.defaultKey; if (!key) continue;`. A provider whose key env is empty is therefore skipped entirely -- it never enters modelClientMap, never becomes a routable model, and never appears in the failover walk. The skip is CORRECT (there is nothing to construct), but it is also COMPLETELY SILENT: the loop logs a line for each provider it DID construct and says nothing at all about the ones it skipped. MEASURED 2026-09-11. OPENAI_WIRE_PROVIDERS registers chutes, groq, mistral and openrouter, and the source comment places groq and mistral deliberately HIGH in the failover walk because the fleet was observed 'burning all four gemini models (each 45s cooling) before ever trying groq's llama-3.3, leaving the funded quota idle'. In this deployment GROQ_API_KEY and MISTRAL_API_KEY are both empty. Across EVERY llm-resolver start recorded in the journal, only 'chutes' and 'openrouter' are logged as constructed; groq and mistral never appear. So the two providers specifically positioned to be the funded fallback have been absent the whole time, and the only way to learn that is to read the provider registry in source and diff it against the journal by hand -- which is what an operator did, and is exactly the work law 6 says should not be absorbed. WHY IT MATTERS RIGHT NOW: the completion plane is dry. anthropic returns 401 invalid key, openrouter reports total_credits 800 against total_usage 800.20, and chutes authenticates then refuses inference with balance $0.0. Every configured provider is terminal, while two providers that are already wired -- and whose vendors issue FREE keys -- sit unconfigured and unmentioned. The cheapest possible repair for a total capability outage was invisible to every surface the system offers. WHAT SHOULD DETECT THIS CLASS WITHOUT AN OPERATOR: at startup, and again whenever the completion advertisement is withdrawn, the resolver should emit the SKIPPED providers as loudly as the constructed ones -- provider id, the env var that was empty, and the model count thereby forfeited. The de-advertisement path is the natural trigger: the moment the vessel says 'all completion providers cooling -- de-advertising llm_completion', it already knows both that it has no capacity AND which named providers it could have had for the price of an env var. Saying the second half there converts a dead-end log line into an actionable one. STRONGER FORM, IF IT IS TO BE AN ACTIVITY RATHER THAN A LOG LINE (law 2): a graded activity that reads the provider registry, reports configured-vs-wired as a shaped impulse, and files a gap when a wired provider has no key. That is selectable, gradable, and composable; a console.warn is none of those. GENERALISE: this is the same shape as every other silent-skip defect in this system -- a guard that fails open and logs only the path it took. The rule is that a component which DECLINES to do something must say what it declined and what that cost, not merely narrate what it did.

WHY PREVIOUS ATTEMPTS ON THIS GAP FAILED (most recent last):
- wrong_location: adversarial refuters agreed 2/2 (conf 0.85, 1.00): While the patch introduces a mechanism to report skipped providers due to missing API keys, it does not address the underlying silent capacity loss a
- semantic_reject: The patch adds a warning for skipped providers but doesn't address the silent capacity loss at startup or provide the required reporting mechanism
- semantic_reject: The patch only adds a warning for skipped providers without fixing the underlying silent capacity loss issue.

Do not repeat these failures. Address the specific cause named above.
